Palladium catalysed, three-component cascade reaction for the efﬁcient
synthesis of diverse small molecules
Jack Herbert, Kelsey Edwards, Visuvanathar Sridharan ⇑
University of Leeds, School of Chemistry, LS2 9JT, UK
article info
Article history:
Received 1 August 2020
Revised 30 September 2020
Accepted 1 October 2020
Available online 8 October 2020
Keywords:
Palladium
Multicomponent
Allene
Crabbé reaction
2-Butene-1,4-diamine
abstract
A palladium catalysed, three-component cascade reaction was employed for the regiospeciﬁc and stere-
oselective synthesis of novel substituted ( Z)-2-butene 1,4-diamine analogues and substituted 4-aryloxy
but-2-enyl amine analogues. Allenes were ﬁrst synthesised from the corresponding alkynes using the
Crabbé reaction and then reacted with a large range of commercially available aryl iodides and amines
to generate a library of small molecules. The reaction is compatible with aryl iodides containing both
electron-donating and electron-withdrawing groups. Amines of different sizes can also be utilised with
no noticeable effect on the yield, regiospeciﬁcity or stereoselectivity.

Introduction
One-pot multicomponent reactions (MCRs) are a powerful
method for synthesizing complex molecular scaffolds in a single
step [1–3]. Advantages in using MCRs over a linear reaction
sequence to afford the same molecule include better yields, ease
of synthetic access to analogues, and a single puriﬁcation step
(Fig. 1 and Fig. 2 ).
Allenes are an underused functionality in organic synthesis, yet
show great potential, as they can react with a vast array of func-
tional groups [4]. The reaction of an aryl palladium(II) intermediate
with an allene yields a highly reactive p-allyl palladium species
which may then undergo an array of transformations. Examples
of attack by nucleophiles [5], electrophiles [6], and transmetalla-
tion [7] have been reported. As part of our ongoing interest in pal-
ladium catalysed cascade chemistry, we herein report the
synthesis of a small library of novel substituted ( Z)-2-butene 1,4-
diamine analogues and substituted 4-aryloxy but-2-enyl amine
analogues, by nucleophilic attack on the p-allyl palladium species
by an amine. A diverse range of amines and aryl iodides were cho-
sen in order to investigate the effects of component sterics and
electronic properties on reaction stereoselectivity and
regioselectivity.
We started our investigation by synthesizing a range of allenes
to be used in the palladium catalysed, three-component cascade
reaction. A total of four allenes were prepared in good yields from
N-propargyl phthalimides and O-propargyl phenols via the Crabbé
reaction ( Scheme 1 ).
The allenes were then used in the palladium catalysed cascade
reaction with a wide array of commercially available amines and
aryl iodides with different steric and electronic properties
(Scheme 2 ).
The reactions of phthalimide based allenes ( 1a and 1b) with a
range of aryl iodides and amines were ﬁrst assessed. Yields ranged
from 31 to 90% and showed high stereoselectivity for the Z-isomer
(Table 1 ). Aryl iodides with both electron-donating and electron-
withdrawing groups are tolerated and had minimal effect on the
yield, stereoselectivity, and regiospeciﬁcity. The products were
obtained as a mixture of inseparable E and Z isomers. The prefer-
ence for Z geometry was established by analogy with similar mole-
cules [8–9]. The E/Z ratio was calculated by comparing the
integrals of the alkenyl protons.
The reaction of phenol based allenes ( 1c and 1d) with a range of
aryl iodides was then assessed. Yields ranged from 31 to 67% with
moderate selectivity for the Z-isomer (Table 2). The yields observed
using the phenol based allenes were comparable to the phthalim-
ide based allenes, however the reaction is less stereoselective.
The proposed reaction mechanism is outlined in Fig. 3. Pd(II) is
ﬁrst reduced to Pd(0) using PPh 3. The aryl iodide then undergoes
oxidative insertion with Pd(0). Allene insertion then displaces
one of the PPh 3 ligands from Pd(0), which is followed by migratory
insertion of the aryl group. The complex can then undergo nucle-
ophilic attack by the amine to liberate the product. The catalyst
can be recovered through reductive elimination by a base [9].

The regiospeciﬁc nature of the reaction can be explained by the
equilibrium of the anti p-allyl complex with the two g1 palladium
complexes (Scheme 3). As expected, the nucleophile preferentially
attacks the less sterically hindered complex to form the a-adduct
[9].
If the c-adduct was obtained, we would expect to see two ger-
minal alkene protons in the 1H NMR spectra. Instead, a single vic-
inal alkene proton appears as a triplet indicating that the a-adduct
is exclusively formed.

The two p-allyl palladium species can interconvert through
rearrangement of the two r-allyl species ( Scheme 4 ). The amine
attacks the least hindered carbon on each p-allyl palladium com-
plex to give a mixture of E/Z isomers. The higher preference for
the Z-isomer seen with the phthalimide based allenes can be
explained by its larger steric bulk, resulting is a more signiﬁcant
clash between the allene R group and the aryl ring in the syn p-
allyl complex This further favours the formation of the anti p-allyl
complex and the resulting Z-isomer [9].
In summary, we have successfully prepared a wide range of
substituted ( Z)-2-butene 1,4-diamine analogues and substituted
4-aryloxy but-2-enyl amine analogues using a palladium catalysed,
three-component cascade reaction, with good yields, regiospeci-
ﬁcity and stereoselectivity for the Z-isomer. A range of aryl iodides
were used, including those with electron-withdrawing and elec-
tron-donating groups. Amines of different steric bulk were also
be used, with no noticeable effect on the yield, regiospeciﬁcity or
stereoselectivity.
